record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a separate single-MLP-neuron approach and reports prompt-detection results, but it does not test or rely on the claim's difference-in-means residual-stream direction.
record.gate_note: The README provides commands and examples for suppressing refusal neurons, but those commands are not evidence that the interventions ran. Its reported detection results measure harmful-versus-harmless prompt discrimination, not refusal behavior. The README also describes generation and attack results, but supplies no extractable generation outcome values here; the multiplier discussion refers to the associated paper's results.
record.test_reason: This is a code-repository README for a single-MLP-neuron refusal paper. It never builds, ablates or adds a difference-in-means residual-stream direction. Its only numeric results are prompt-detection AUROCs from one neuron's activations, which are not refusal rates. Generation and attack-success results appear only as figures, or are attributed to the paper, with no readable values. Nothing in the text bears on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README presents the work as showing that suppressing one MLP neuron bypasses safety alignment in Qwen3 (1.7B–32B) and Llama-3.1 (8B, 70B), and that the neuron's activations detect harmful prompts. It does not discuss the residual-stream refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes ranking and intervening on individual MLP neurons using contrastive gradient and activation scores, rather than finding and ablating a harmful-minus-harmless mean residual-stream direction. Repository type: reproduction code for the associated single-neuron paper.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says attack success varies with multiplier magnitude, with an inverted-U trend, but gives no extractable numerical outcome by setting in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: One refusal-neuron activation discriminates harmful from harmless prompts: AUROC 0.87–0.97 across four datasets on Llama-3.1-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single MLP neuron's activation at post-instruction tokens encodes prompt harmfulness well enough for detection.

fits_no_version.finding: The README states that clamping a single MLP neuron bypasses refusal across Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 models. ASR has an inverted-U relation with multiplier magnitude because coherence degrades. No readable values are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be bypassed by intervening on one MLP neuron, with a trade-off between attack success and coherence.

record.problems: The README reports detection metrics without uncertainty estimates. Generation instructions and referenced figures do not provide extractable intervention outcome values in the supplied text; the code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No generation-ASR rows included: README commands are instructions, and the multiplier-sweep description refers to results without giving per-model or per-condition values in the supplied text. No rows for the paper's reported 77.0% and 76.4% ASR comparison because the README explicitly attributes those figures to the paper's original run, rather than reporting a repository-run result.

untested.parts: Difference-in-means direction, its ablation and addition, and capability retention: none tested. A single-neuron intervention is a different object.
No weight edit or abliteration result.
No link between jailbreaks and the direction, and no adversarial training.
No multi-direction, affine or cone analysis. A neuron-level mechanism is implied but not compared with the direction.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No transfer of the refusal direction. The cross-language remark concerns a self-harm concept neuron.
No comparison of training methods or stages.
Qwen3 is run with thinking disabled; no reasoning-mode test.

missing.what: Per-model HarmBench/JBB ASR for single-neuron suppression (constant and anchor modes) and the multiplier sweep. Shown only in figures or in the associated paper (arXiv:2605.08513), not readable here.
missing.locator: README figures attack_asr.png, rank_comparison_combined.png; associated paper

record.verdict_notes: The repository was created and pushed on the same date and is a paper-reproduction artefact. The associated paper may compare neurons with the refusal direction and should be read separately for possible V1/V4 relevance. The README does not cite the original refusal-direction paper.

versions.untested_parts: The residual-stream difference-in-means direction, all-layer/all-position ablation, induced harmless-request refusal, and preservation of other abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No attack suppression of the claimed direction or training against its ablation is tested.
The README does not test affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
Prompt discrimination using a neuron's activations does not test whether harmfulness judgment is separate from refusal decision.
No transfer of the claimed direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.
No test of the claimed direction in reasoning models is reported.
